newsitem.title: USA: Neutral Zone, W African crude offered into US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Neutral Zone, W African crude offered into US Gulf.

text.p: Foreign crude offerings into the U.S. Gulf Coast were subdued on Friday, with talk focused on Neutral Zone and West African barrels, traders said.
A U.S. major was heard offering Ratawi and Eocene crudes from the Neutral Zone between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. The cargoes were expected to arrive around late June-early July, traders said.
Traders valued the heavy sour crudes around $5.00 a barrel discount to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, although no firm asking numbers were disclosed.
From West Africa, a U.S. major was offering Nigerian Qua Iboe for June 18-23 arrival. The grade was assessed around dated Brent plus 45 cents a barrel.
Brass River was also looking for a home, with the asking price around WTI plus 25 cents a barrel.
Traders noted that West African barrels have been fetching higher prices lately as a result of increased Far East and Mediterranean buying.
Recent ethnic clashes in Nigeria may also have pumped up the price, traders said.
Royal Dutch/Shell, the country's largest equity producer, cut some 20 percent of Forcados output, or some 90,000 barrels per day (bpd), as a result of the renewed unrest.
The company declared force majeure, with liftings from April 29 expected to be delayed by two to three days.
The June spread between WTI and Brent narrowed on Friday to around $1.50-60 a barrel, down some 10 cents from Thursday.

Elsewhere, an equity producer sold a Cusiana cargo, the last available for May loading, to a U.S. refiner for loading around May 17-18. The price was undisclosed, although the gasoline-rich grade was last done at around WTI minus $1.55-60 a barrel.
One trader pegged the latest price at WTI minus $1.67 a barrel, but this level could not be immediately confirmed.
